_comment: Input schema for build_fcf_workbook.py. Example Co is a made-up company: every number below is invented, but the lines re-add to reported_ocf so the tie-out passes. Copy this file, swap in a real company's data, and run the builder. Every value is copied straight off the statement of cash flows exactly how the company printed it (uses of cash negative). Set 'fcf': true on any adjustment you decide to subtract from normalized FCF. Set 'is_sbc': true on the stock-based comp line. Working-capital lines are auto-flagged one-time + fcf, so just list them.
_non_us_notes: For non-US / IFRS filers: (1) set 'units' to the reporting currency, e.g. '(EUR in Millions)', and keep the ENTIRE model (incl. market_cap/enterprise_value) in that currency. (2) If the statement starts from something other than net income (IFRS indirect method usually starts from 'Profit before tax' or 'Operating profit'), put that figure in 'net_income' and add a top-level 'starting_label' string, e.g. "starting_label": "Profit before tax". The builder uses it for the label; default is 'Net Income'.

adjustments.label: Depreciation and amortization
adjustments.rationale: Non-cash; kept added back. Real reinvestment is captured separately through Capital Expenditures.

adjustments.label: Stock-based compensation
adjustments.rationale: Real dilutive cost that GAAP adds back as non-cash. Subtract it.

adjustments.label: Deferred income taxes
adjustments.rationale: YOUR CALL. Fill in from your own judgment card.

adjustments.label: Other
adjustments.rationale: JUDGMENT CHECKPOINT. Open the footnotes, see what is inside the number, and decide. Not decided in this example.

capex_rationale: Purchases of property, plant and equipment.
_valuation_note: Optional valuation footer. market_cap: from a live quote (record the date in valuation_date). enterprise_value: market_cap + total debt - cash & equivalents, from the latest balance sheet. With enterprise_value set, the builder emits the full footer (Market Cap, EV, average FCF and yields, last-year FCF yield, NI Delta). Every yield divides by MIN(market cap, EV).
